title: 21 CFR part 7 recalls: definitions, classification, depth, and the recall communication a consignee receives
rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 7.3(g) a recall is a firm's removal or correction of a marketed product that FDA considers to be in violation of the laws it administers and against which the agency would initiate legal action, and it does not include a market withdrawal (7.3(j): a distributed product involving a minor violation that would not be subject to legal action, or no violation) or a stock recovery (7.3(k): a product that has not been marketed or has not left the direct control of the firm). Under 7.3(m) FDA assigns a recall classification indicating the relative degree of health hazard: Class I, a reasonable probability that use of or exposure to the product will cause serious adverse health consequences or death; Class II, use or exposure may cause temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences or the probability of serious adverse health consequences is remote; Class III, use or exposure is not likely to cause adverse health consequences. A consignee under 7.3(n) is anyone who received, purchased, or used the product being recalled. 21 CFR 7.40 states that recall is a voluntary action and that 7.40 through 7.59 provide guidance; recall may be undertaken voluntarily by manufacturers and distributors or at FDA's request (7.40(b), 7.45, 7.46). Under 7.42(b)(1) the recall strategy specifies the depth of recall: the consumer or user level, the retail level, or the wholesale level. Under 7.49 the recalling firm is responsible for promptly notifying each affected direct account; the communication conveys that the product is subject to a recall, that further distribution or use of remaining product should cease immediately, where appropriate that the direct account should notify its customers who received the product, and instructions on what to do with the product, and it should identify the product, size, lot numbers, codes or serial numbers. Under 7.49(d) consignees that receive a recall communication should immediately carry out the instructions set forth by the recalling firm and, where necessary, extend the recall to their consignees. Under 7.50 FDA lists each new recall in the weekly FDA Enforcement Report.
exam_relevance: Tests the recall vocabulary a pharmacy meets on a recall notice (class, depth, market withdrawal, stock recovery) and the guidance-level expectation that a consignee carries out the recalling firm's instructions.

authority.name: FDA, Understanding Drug Recalls: What to Know and What to Do

common_confusions: Class I is the most serious class and Class III the least.
The classification describes health hazard; the depth of recall is a separate element of the recall strategy.
Sections 7.40 through 7.59 are framed as guidance, and 7.49(d) says consignees should carry out the recalling firm's instructions.
A market withdrawal and a stock recovery are not recalls under 7.3(g).
verification_notes: Read on 2026-09-17 in 21 CFR part 7 on eCFR and on FDA's Understanding Drug Recalls page (content current as of 05/06/2026), which states that a recall may be recommended or requested by FDA or initiated voluntarily at any time by a company and that FDA's role is to oversee the company's recall strategy.
